thread:
maya: Heads up — nightly GPU smoke on h100-canary turned red for shard 42.
maya: Quick log snippet below, looks like a kernel launch failure + OOM interleaved.
maya: ```
[   12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:01.0): 79, pid=4821, GPU has fallen off the bus
[   12.345690] nvidia: GPU lockup - aborting.
[   12.346001] cudaError: invalid device function
[   12.346500] oom-killer: killing process 4821 (inference) score 987
```
maya: I kicked a rerun but wanted to ping infra/owners in case this is driver-related.
ci-bot: Build #12584 (h100-canary, shard=42) rerun queued: https://ci.internal/12584
dinesh: Thx. Did this start after the driver canary rollout yesterday?
maya: I _think_ the roll was merged ~22:15 UTC yesterday by infra (driver 535.102 -> 536.12). Logs from other shards are mostly ok but 42 and 44 show the NVRM/Xid pattern.
alex: Noted. Can someone grab the node's dmesg + nvidia-smi output before it reboots? Often we lose the trace.
julia: I have a copy from one of the failing jobs: link -> s3://internal-ci/logs/12584/shard42/dmesg.txt
julia: dmesg shows multiple `invalid device function` entries and then the process OOM. No kdump present.
dinesh: If it's driver-side, can we repro with the pinned image locally? maya, can you rerun the failing shard with `driver.pin=535.86`? quick experiment.
maya: Trying a targeted rerun now with pin -> /pipelines/12584?shard=42&driver=535.86
infra-bot: Rerun submitted: pipeline 12584.rerun.3 (driver=535.86) — ETA ~8m
sam: If the older driver fixes it, we should bisect the driver bump — but first check whether the PR touches any CUDA kernels or custom ops.
maya: The PR list for this CI run: PR#4212 (model-quant), PR#4219 (ci: infra pin), PR#4220 (noop lint). None touch custom kernels.
alex: Good. Then driver is suspicious. Also ask buildbot to capture full nvbug logs on next failure: `NVIDIA_SAVE_APB=1` env.
julia: FYI the core dump size limit is low on agents, we don't persist cores. We should enable `persist-coredump: true` for canary nodes while triaging.
dinesh: Agreed — I'll flip that for the canary pool; won't affect prod.
maya: Rerun finished: pipeline 12584.rerun.3 -> still failed with same stack. dmesg attached: s3://.../12584/rerun3/dmesg.txt
maya: Quick grep: repeated `invalid device function` followed by `gpu reset` and then oom of worker.
sam: Two paths: 1) driver regression — roll back on canary, file infra bug to bisect upstream driver; 2) workload regression — check memory shape differences for this shard.
alex: Can we repro the exact workload locally on a repro node? Maya — can you upload the request payload for shard 42 and the model binary used by the runner?
maya: Uploaded: s3://.../12584/shard42/payload.json and model @ s3://.../models/run-2026-03-16-v2.tar
julia: I'll spin a repro node with driver 536.12 and try the workload. If I get invalid-device-function locally, we can file a proper bug with NVIDIA and start a bisect.
ci-bot: Reminder: attach `--collect-nv-trace` to the job for the next run to get PTX/JIT traces.
dinesh: For now, reverting the driver on canary to 535.86 to stop noisy failures. I'll start a staged rollback.
alex: +1. After rollback, let's run a full canary smoke matrix overnight and if stable, schedule a driver-bisect with NVIDIA support on Monday.
maya: Thanks all — will keep this thread updated. If anyone gets repro locally, post logs here and I'll open infra ticket.
sam: One more ask: add a quick flaky-test label to the PRs that triggered these so downstream triage knows not to escalate immediately.
maya: Done. PR#4212 marked flaky-triage.
julia: Update: I reproduced the `invalid device function` on a repro node with 536.12; collecting nvtrace and will open NV support ticket with logs + repro steps.
maya: Great — marking as triage-in-progress, and I've pinned canary back to 535.86. Will update when NV reply arrives. :eyes:
